evidence: Ter. Haut. 211: Ego ībō hinc intrō
terms.comment: Also of a cause, “from this”: hinc illae lacrimae, so that explains the tears (Ter. And. 126). With illinc: on this side … on that.

phrases.latin: Ego ībō hinc intrō, ut videam nōbīs quid cēnae siet. Tū … vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius.
phrases.english: I’ll go in and see what we have for dinner. You, … mind you don’t wander too far from here.

phrases.latin: Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō. — Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.
phrases.english: Invite me to dinner. — I do indeed. — Let’s go in, then. — Agreed.

phrases.latin: pōma sumus Cybelēs: procul hinc discēde, viātor, nē cadat in miserum nostra ruīna caput
phrases.english: we are Cybele’s fruit: keep well away from here, traveller, or we may fall on your poor head

phrases.latin: attat! hoc illud est: hinc illae lacrimae
phrases.english: aha! so that’s it: hence those tears
